gene symbol: MTHFR [60]. gene name: MTHFR [63]. The protein encoded by this gene catalyzes the conversion of 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, a co-substrate for homocysteine remethylation to methionine [69]. Genetic variation in this gene influences susceptibility to occlusive vascular disease, neural tube defects, colon cancer and acute leukemia, and mutations in this gene are associated with methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase deficiency.[provided by RefSeq, Oct 2009] [69].

pubmed title: ACMG Practice Guideline: lack of evidence for MTHFR polymorphism testing [61]. pubmed title: Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase and psychiatric diseases [67]. pubmed title: Shifting landscapes of human MTHFR missense-variant effects [73]. pubmed title: MTHFR gene polymorphisms in diabetes mellitus [78]. pubmed title: Increased methylation levels of the MTHFR gene promoter in Down syndrome [83]. MTHFR polymorphism testing is frequently ordered by physicians as part of the clinical evaluation for thrombophilia [88]. It was previously hypothesized that reduced enzyme activity of MTHFR led to mild hyperhomocysteinemia which led to an increased risk for venous thromboembolism, coronary heart disease, and recurrent pregnancy loss [88]. Recent meta-analyses have disproven an association between hyperhomocysteinemia and risk for coronary heart disease and between MTHFR polymorphism status and risk for v [88]. Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) is a key enzyme for the critical process of one-carbon metabolism involving folate and homocysteine metabolisms [90]. It is known that some polymorphism of MTHFR would result in reduction of MTHFR enzyme activity as well as DNA methylation process, later shown to have significant impacts in various psychiatric diseases [90]. However, it is unclear whether the polymorphism of MTHFR could be an independent or an add-on risk factor for specific psychiatric symptoms [90]. Most rare clinical missense variants cannot currently be classified as pathogenic or benign [92]. Deficiency in human 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR), the most common inherited disorder of folate metabolism, is caused primarily by rare missense variants [92]. Further complicating variant interpretation, variant impacts often depend on environment [92]. An important example of this phenomenon is the MTHFR variant p.Ala222Val (c.665C>T), which is carried by half of all humans and has a phenotypi [92]. The methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR), methionine synthase (MTR), and methionine synthase reductase (MTRR) are three regulatory enzymes in the folic acid (FA) cycle play a critical role in the balance of methionine and homocysteine [94]. MTHFR and MTRR gene polymorphisms affect the biochemical activities of enzymes, impairing the remethylation of homocysteine to methionine [94]. In 1972, severe MTHFR deficiency resulting in homocystinuria was first reported, suggesting MTHFR involvement in the d [94]. MTHFR is a key enzyme in the one-carbon metabolic pathway, whose activity has been implicated in Down syndrome (DS) and in the development of congenital heart defects (CHDs) [96]. The main aim was to assess promoter methylation levels of the MTHFR gene in DS individuals, including those with congenital heart defects (DS-CHD+), and those without (DS-CHD-), as well as control subjects [96]. We also investigated if common MTHFR polymorphisms, namely 677C > T and 1298A > C correlate with MTHFR promoter methyl [96].
